name: Aaron Sawit
description: Aaron Sawit is a security engineer in Singapore who builds free learning tools used by students and teachers, runs his own infrastructure, and explains hard things simply.
about: I work in cybersecurity full time, on the risk and compliance side, and I tutor special needs students on the side. The tutoring is why the Versed tools exist and why they are free: the kids I teach needed calmer, simpler tools than the ones schools pay for, so I built them.

My training is hands-on. I hold the GIAC Certified Incident Handler and worked through Hack The Box's SOC analyst path. I like the moment a vague symptom turns into one specific line in one specific log.
Six years of teaching children who struggle with text has made me good at one thing most engineers avoid: explaining something hard to someone who is not technical, without talking down to them.

also.name: pdf-redaction-check
also.what: Checks whether the redacted text in a PDF is actually gone. Finds words still sitting under black boxes, including boxes stamped on as overlays, and redaction marks that were never applied. Built after it caught a real document my first version missed.

also.name: llm-guardrail-tests
also.what: Regression tests for the guardrails on your own AI feature: 20 known prompt-injection patterns, graded deterministically with random markers and a canary, no judge model, ready for CI.

also.name: model-diff-audit
also.what: Bit-level comparison of an AI model against the base it claims to come from, separating ordinary fine-tuning from tampering. On a real tampered model it found the 90 edited rows out of 151,936.

also.name: toolcall-probe
also.what: Asks a local model endpoint directly whether it really calls tools or only describes them, and says which layer is at fault.

also.name: cctokens
also.what: Shows where Claude Code tokens go: usage and API-equivalent cost by day, model and project. One Python file, no dependencies, nothing leaves the machine. Counts each message once, which the logs do not.

also.name: docker-gpu-reload-check
also.what: Finds containers that will silently lose their NVIDIA GPU on the next systemd reload, and prints the fix. Read-only, tested against my own two-GPU server.

also.name: private-relay-block
also.what: Puts Apple devices back on the network's DNS filter by blocking iCloud Private Relay the way Apple documents, plus the cached relay addresses. Dry-run and clean undo.

also.name: disc-image-id
also.what: Identifies Xbox, PS1 and PS2 disc images by signature instead of file extension, and converts the full Xbox dumps that the xemu emulator rejects. Tested, open source.

also.name: Exam-practice tutoring app
also.what: Student and teacher web app for primary school English, built with a partner who owns the backend. Hint ladders that fade as mastery grows, and a teacher view of every attempt. In development.

fit.title: Detection and response
fit.text: Log analysis, SIEM work and incident handling. I write detections other people can read and test, and I investigate until there is one named cause.

fit.title: Security-minded infrastructure
fit.text: Linux, containers, networking and monitoring, run as code with backups I have restored from and a threat model I can explain.

fit.title: Shipping secure products
fit.text: I take products from a blank page to real users on Cloudflare's edge, and make the privacy and abuse decisions as part of the design.

seeking: Security engineering, detection engineering and platform security roles

cv.summary: Security engineer with a First Class computer science degree and the GCIH. By day I assess technology risk against government security policy. I also build and test AI systems: a marking system measured against human examiners, open-source guardrail tests, and a suite of free learning tools used by students. Six years of tutoring special needs students taught me to explain hard things simply.

AWS Bedrock and IAM, Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, D1, KV and Pages, TypeScript, authentication and sessions, rate limiting, CSP and security headers

experience.title: Cybersecurity Engineer
points: Assess the security risk of SaaS and third-party services that government agencies want to adopt, against government ICT security policy (IM8).
Review requests to deviate from policy: weigh the risk, check the compensating controls, and recommend whether to approve, reject or change them.
Point of contact for agencies' security policy questions. I turn policy text into a clear answer that engineers can act on.

experience.title: AI Engineer (assignment)
points: Rebuilt an early prototype into a working AI marking system for the group's bootcamp selection exam: Python, Claude on AWS Bedrock (3.5 Sonnet, later Sonnet 4), versioned prompt templates, and parallel marking of a full intake from a spreadsheet.
Wrote the evaluation harness that scores the model against instructor marking, and used it to drive every prompt change: agreement rose from about 60% to about 77%.
Used it on past papers and live applicants, several hundred scripts in all.

Earned the GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH) through SANS SEC504 and completed the Hack The Box SOC Analyst path.
